title: Design-Build of a Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) Trailer
description: Amendment 0002 The purpose for Amendment 0002 is to change the time offers are due from 2 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) to 8 a.m. ET and the due date to September 15th, 2026. Any submission received after September 15th, 2026 at 8 a.m Eastern Time (ET) will not be eligible for award. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) intends to award a single-award, Firm-Fixed-Price, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) systems. The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a contract vehicle for the design, engineering, manufacturing, integration, testing, and production of trailer-based mobile command post systems capable of supporting FBI command, control, communications, and computer (C4) operations. The Tier II MCPV requirement consists of a custom-integrated gooseneck trailer system and, when ordered, a compatible Class 4 prime hauler vehicle. The MCPV Trailer shall provide a mobile operational environment supporting mission communications, networking, workspace, power generation and distribution, environmental control, equipment racks, audio/visual capabilities, RF and satellite connectivity provisions, security systems, and integration of Government-furnished and Contractor-furnished mission equipment. The contract will include a First Article requirement. The Contractor shall design, manufacture, integrate, test, and obtain Government approval of an initial MCPV Trailer configuration prior to production quantities. The approved First Article configuration will establish the production baseline for subsequent MCPV Trailer systems. The Government anticipates ordering approximately thirteen (13) MCPV trailer systems and associated prime hauler vehicles over the contract ordering period; however, the Government guarantees only the minimum contract obligation identified in the solicitation. The maximum contract value shall not exceed $15,000,000.00.

title: FORNITURA DI FERRAMENTA COMPRENSIVO DI TRASPORTO (CONSEGNA) PER PRODUZIONI TELEVISIVE DEL CPTV DI ROMA, MILANO, TORINO E NAPOLI
description: Accordo Quadro con un unico operatore ai sensi dell’art. 59 comma 3 del Codice avente ad oggetto la fornitura di ferramenta comprensiva di trasporto (consegna) per produzioni televisive del CPTV di Roma, Milano, Torino e Napoli. La lista del materiale oggetto di fornitura è riportata nel dettaglio all'interno della documentazione di gara. La fornitura è comprensiva delle schede tecniche e di sicurezza dei materiali forniti e delle dichiarazioni di conformità rilasciate dal produttore a norma di legge nonchè di ogni onere relativo al trasporto e recapito ad uno dei magazzini Rai di Roma, Milano, Napoli o Torino. Rai stipulerà con l’aggiudicatario un Accordo Quadro della durata di 36 mesi decorrenti dalla data di sottoscrizione dell’accordo quadro, per effetto del quale l’affidatario si obbligherà ad eseguire le prestazioni oggetto dell’appalto, secondo le specifiche tecniche oggetto del Capitolato ai prezzi unitari offerti. I documenti di gara conterranno le seguenti previsioni ai sensi dell'art. 120, comma 1, lett. a) del Codice: - qualora l'importo contrattuale non dovesse essere esaurito alla scadenza del termine di durata contrattuale, la durata dell’ accordo quadro potrà essere estesa per il tempo necessario all’utilizzo dell’intero importo contrattuale (fermo restando la natura non vincolante delle prestazioni); - in caso di necessità nel corso della vigenza contrattuale, Rai si riserva di modificare ai sensi dell’art. 120 comma1 lett. a) del Codice di modificare/compensare la capienza dimensionale di ciascuna voce contrattuale. In particolare, Rai, a seconda di esigenze specifiche, dovute al maggior impiego di una voce contrattuale rispetto ad un’altra potrà operare la riduzione della voce meno utilizzata in favore dell’aumento della voce più utilizzata, fermo restando il valore complessivo dell’ accordo quadro; - la facoltà di richiedere all’appaltatore, nel corso della durata dell’accordo quadro, qualora i si renda necessario un aumento o una diminuzione delle prestazioni fino a concorrenza del quinto dell'importo del contratto pari ad euro 63.480, anche ai sensi dell’art. 120, comma 9, del Codice, di imporre all'appaltatore l’esecuzione alle condizioni originariamente previste. In tal caso l'appaltatore non può fare valere il diritto alla risoluzione dell’accordo quadro. In casi eccezionali, al verificarsi delle condizioni indicate all’art. 120 comma 11 del Codice, la durata dell’Accordo Quadro anche se prorogata nei termini sopra descritti ma ancora in corso di esecuzione, potrà essere ulteriormente prorogata per il tempo strettamente necessario alla conclusione della procedura di individuazione del nuovo contraente (ferma restando la natura non vincolante dell’importo residuo nei termini sopra espressi). In tal caso l’appaltatore sarà tenuto all’esecuzione delle prestazioni oggetto dell’accordo quadro agli stessi prezzi, patti e condizioni previsti nel contratto.

title: NHSGGC Walk & Talk Service
description: The aim of the service is to provide short-term, non-clinical support to young people who may be experiencing anxiety, low mood, isolation or other issues, and who may be disengaged from education and/or the community. Through regular contact with an identified staff member or trained volunteer, outside of their home, young people are supported over a number of weeks to gain confidence, re-engage with their peers or services, and work towards positive destinations. The service will provide or support pathways to appropriate positive destinations, for example through their own services or through partner services in the local area.

title: Pavilion Design and Fabrication Services - at GULFOOD 2027
description: Agriculture & Agri-Food Canada (AAFC), is seeking proposals for Pavilion Design and Fabrication services at GULFOOD 2027. AAFC is organizing the Canada Pavilion at GULFOOD 2027, which will be held at the Dubai World Trade Center and the Dubai Exposition Center, Expo City, in Dubai, UAE from March 15 to 19, 2027. The Canada Pavilion will host a number of Canadian agri-food companies, associations, and federal/provincial departments. GULFOOD is the world's largest annual food and hospitality show. Held in Dubai, UAE, the show attracts approximately 8,500 exhibitors participating from over 195 countries and 200,000 professional visitors. AAFC’s Canada Pavilion Program provides Canadian food exporters with the opportunity to raise awareness of their products and position themselves competitively via the use of the Canada Brand. The key attributes of the Canada Brand are quality, innovation, sustainability and diversity. Canada’s Pavilion design should aim to support the promotion of these attributes. Bids must include the following: 1. Executive Summary: A brief overview of the proposed concept and design, key milestones and timelines for delivery of the project, and overall outcomes to be achieved. 2. Design Concept: The bid will include a design layout for an 866 square metre (sq. m) Canada Pavilion spread across four halls at two separate venues. One (1) 33m x 6m stand (198 sq. m), one (1) 17m x 6m stand (102 sq. m) and one (1) 23m x 6m stand (138 sq. m) in the Rice, Pulses & Grains Hall (Expo City Dubai), one (1) 33m x 6m stand (198 sq.) and two (2) 3m x 13m stand (39 sq.) in the World Food Hall (Expo City Dubai), one (1) 12m x 8m stand (96 sq. m) in the Meat Hall (Dubai World Trade Centre), and one (1) 7m x 8m stand (56 sq. m) in the Dairy Hall (Dubai World Trade Centre). The design concept must leverage existing Canada Brand colour schemes, logos, taglines and make the Canada Pavilion stand out from other countries/competitors on the show floor. The design concept must showcase the attributes associated to the Canada Brand (quality, sustainability, innovation and diversity as they apply to the agriculture and food sector) and allow the Canada Pavilion to stand out from other countries/competitors on the show floor. The design must allow for a combination of enclosed and open concept booth layouts to accommodate the needs of both individual companies as well as larger group exhibitors. The design and layout of the pavilion should be flexible to accommodate changes from year-to-year. The design should include sustainable materials that can be reused throughout the duration of the contract. 3. Project Management for Services: Provide a detailed description of the approach, human resources required for each service and detailed, comprehensive timelines including milestones for planning and interactions with Show Authority, AAFC and exhibitors as well as fabrication and delivery schedule. 4. Contingency Plan: Describe potential challenges, constraints or unexpected situations and/or major difficulties that may arise during the course of the project including staffing issues and provide mitigating measures and approaches to address these. 5. Summary/Recommendation: Provide any additional information and/or recommendations that are essential to the project.

title: 5A015-246691 - Medevac Air Charters Services

title: Wood Islands Containment Cell, Wood Islands, PEI
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC), on behalf of Transport Canada (TC), has a requirement to construct new containment cell at Wood Islands Ferry Terminal, Wood Islands, Queens County, Prince Edward Island. The scope of work generally includes the installation and maintenance of environmental controls, partial removal, stockpiling, and placement of existing armour stone, local dredging and displacement of soft material, new perimeter containment cell berm and civil works to update the existing site drainage. All work is to be performed in accordance with the plans and specifications for Project Number: R.1384200.001 forming part of the bid document. The estimated cost for this opportunity is within the following cost category: between $5,000,001 to $20,000,000 (HST included)

title: 6550--Notice of Intent to Sole Source; Qiagen LLC
description: This is a notice of intent to award a sole source contract and is not a request for quotes. The Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA) Network Contracting Office NCO2, on behalf of VISN2 South Medical Centers, intends to award a Firm Fixed Price (FFP), sole source action to: Name of Contractor: QIAGEN LLC Street Address: 19300 Germantown Road City, State, Zip: Germantown, MD 20874-1415 VISN02 medical centers have a recurring requirement for US Food & Drug Administration (FDA) approved In Vitro Diagnostic (IVD), cell mediated immunity (IGRA) tests for detecting Mycobacterium infections using chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA) on LIAISON analyzers. Market research was conducted in accordance with FAR Part 10, reviewing the offerings and capabilities available through the current marketplace. In accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 6.103-1, it has been determined that only one source is reasonably available, QIAGEN LLC. QIAGEN is the manufacturer and sole distributor of the QuantiFERON TB Gold testing. QuantiFERON is the only test capable of meeting the salient characteristics of the requirement and providing the necessary compatibility with the Department of Veterans Affairs existing LIAISON analyzers. Market research failed to produce additional sources capable of fulfilling this requirement as a whole; No subcontracting opportunities are available for this requirement. In accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) this notice of intent to sole source with justification to limit sources, satisfies the public posting requirements. Veterans Health Administration prohibits the use of gray market items in their Medical Centers. Gray market items are considered to be items outside of the original equipment manufacturer s intended distribution channels. This notice is not a request for quotes; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement which shall be considered by the Government. All capability statements must be received by no later than 10:00 AM Eastern Standard Time on September 15, 2025. Responses to be submitted to Lindsay Goldsmith, Contracting Officer at lindsay.goldsmith@va.gov. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: MRTC Parking Lot Refresh
description: Marine Forces Special Operations Command, (MARSOC), Marine Raider Center (MRC), Camp Lejeune, NC has a requirement to repair/fill cracks and seal approximately 130,000 square feet of parking lot at RR450 parking lots. The general scope of work includes cleaning, filling, smoothing, and sealing both parking lots around RR450. The following Objectives are provided: 1. Mandatory Site Visit and Base Access Requirements A mandatory site visit will be conducted on 27 August at 0900 EST at the Building RR450 parking lot, Stone Bay, MCB Camp Lejeune, NC. Mandatory Attendance: Attendance at this site visit is mandatory. Only those vendors who attend the site visit in its entirety will be eligible to submit quotes in response to this solicitation. Quotes received from vendors who did not attend the site visit will be rejected without evaluation. Base Access Request Deadline: To gain access to the MARFORSOC compound at Stone Bay, contractor personnel must be vetted. Vendors must submit their base access request documentation to the Contracting Officer (Samuel Williams) and the Contract Specialist via email no later than 24 August. Access Request Content: The access request must be submitted on the visiting company's official stationery, signed by a company authority, and contain the following information for each attendee (limit of 2 attendees per company): Full Legal Name (Last, First, Middle) Date of Birth Place of Birth Citizenship Driver's License Number and State of Issuance 2. Questions Offerors shall submit all questions regarding this solicitation via email to the POCs listed below no later than 10:00AM EST on September 9, 2026. The Government will consolidate all questions and issue an official amendment on SAM.gov. Contracting Officer: Krissia Avelares Valle (krissia.i.avelaresvalle.mil@socom.mil) Contracting Specialist: Spenser Gagnon (spenser.e.gagnon.civ@socom.mil) 3. Proposal Submission Instructions Eligible offerors (who attended the mandatory site visit) shall submit their proposals via email to the Contracting Office. Proposals must be submitted in three (3) separate and distinct volumes as outlined below. Page limits must be strictly adhered to; any pages exceeding the limit will not be evaluated. All proposals are due Volume Title Page Limit Submission Requirements Volume I Technical Capability 6 Pages Max Technical Approach, Equipment List, Personnel Overview, and Draft Construction Phasing Plan. Volume II Past Performance 2 Pages Max Up to three (3) Past Performance References of similar scope and complexity. Volume III Price No Limit Completed SF 1449 Schedule of Supplies/Services, Price Breakdown, and Representations & Certifications. 4. Volume Content Requirements A. Volume I: Technical Capability The Technical Volume must clearly demonstrate the offeror's capability to perform the requirements set forth in the Statement of Work (SOW). Boilerplate or repeating the SOW language without detail is unacceptable. The volume must include: Technical Approach: A detailed narrative describing how the offeror will execute SOW Objectives #1 through #6, specifically outlining the crack cleaning process, crack-filling application (Objective #2), seal coat application and mixing ratio (Objective #3), restriping and stenciling (Objective #4), parking block replacement and installation (Objective #5), and the handicap sign post installations (Objective #6). Draft Construction Phasing Plan: A draft plan showing how the offeror will execute the work while maintaining at least fifty percent (50%) parking capacity operational continuity at Building RR450 at all times. The plan must include a tentative Gantt chart schedule within the 120-day Period of Performance and explain how emergency vehicle access will be guaranteed. Security and Base Access Compliance: A brief statement acknowledging and demonstrating a plan to comply with Camp Lejeune base access regulations (NCIC checks) and coordinating with MARSOC-provided escorts. B. Volume II: Past Performance Offerors shall submit up to three (3) past performance references for federal, state, local, or commercial contracts executed within the past three (3) years that are similar in scope and complexity to the RR450 requirement (e.g., parking lot sealing, crack filling, and striping requirements exceeding 50,000 sq ft). Each reference must include: Contract Number, Customer Name, and Point of Contact (Email and Phone). Period of Performance and Total Contract Dollar Value. A brief description of the work performed, highlighting similarities to the RR450 scope of work, specifically mentioning the total square footage treated and whether phasing or escort requirements were managed. Note: Offerors may submit standard reference letters in lieu of, or in addition to, the contact list. C. Volume III: Price The offeror shall submit a fully completed SF 1449 schedule with firm-fixed-prices (FFP) for the single, lump-sum CLIN (0001). The offeror must also submit a supporting price breakdown detailing direct material costs, direct labor costs (complying with Davis-Bacon Wage Determination No. NC20260090), mobilization, project management/overhead, and bond costs.

L'établissement a été construit en 1960 pour les bâtiments A, C et D, en 1980 pour le bâtiment B, l'ensemble possède une surface utile de 15 175 m². title: Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM) At Surf City, North Carolina - Industry Day
description: Special Notice: W912PM27BA001 Title: Industry Day for FY26/FY 27 Coastal Storm Risk Management Surf City, North Carolina The Industry Day Meeting for the Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM) Surf City will occur on 15 September 2026 at 11:00 AM EST via Teams. The work consists of furnishing plant, labor, materials, and equipment to perform dredging, transporting, placing and shaping beach fill and performing all pre and post construction beach surveys. Approximately 1 borrow areas is available for the project and located offshore of Topsail Island Beaches at the south end of the island. The Surf City Coastal Storm Risk Management Project consists of placing 6,500,000 CY of Dune and Berm beach fill along approximately 33,300 LF of Surf City Beach. This project shall use either an ocean certified hopper and/or an ocean certified pipeline dredge. The project also consists of extending approximately 40 existing walkover structures in Surf City and the stabilization of approximately 46 to 56 acres of new dune. In addition, breakout sessions will be provided with individual contractors following the group industry day meeting. Please indicate with your RSVP if you would like to request a breakout meeting. Please RSVP no later than 3PM ET 11 September 2026 to both Ros Shoemaker and Jenifer Garland at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and jenifer.m.garland@usace.army.mil if you plan to attend the Industry Day and/or request a breakout session. A Teams calendar invite will be sent out to all RSVP�s.

description: Le marché envisagé a pour objet la fourniture de liaisons de dépannage, pouvant notamment être mises en oeuvre dans l’hypothèse d’évènements climatiques extrêmes entrainant des avaries sur le réseau électrique. 2 liaisons seront livrées dans le cadre du marché envisagé (en 2027). Il est prévu de solliciter la fourniture de modules et accessoires permettant l’installation de lignes de secours aériennes constituées de mâts haubanés d’une longueur totale de 2,5 kilomètres en faisceau double (câble conducteur de section 570 mm2) pour chaque liaison, chaque portée ayant une longueur minimale de 250 mètres. De manière accessoire, les matériels livrés doivent permettre la mise en œuvre de configurations de lignes différentes (lignes de longueur moindre, avec un nombre de mâts d’ancrage/de suspension différent). RTE a également identifié que l’amont industriel est en mesure de proposer des matériels permettant l’installation de lignes de secours en faisceau triple. Aussi, il est envisagé de solliciter auprès des fournisseurs invités à participer à la consultation la remise de propositions portant sur cette solution. Il convient de noter que les prestations envisagées n’ont pas pour objet la fourniture de câbles conducteurs et d’entretoises.

Receives a rating of �Acceptable� on the Technical Capability evaluation factor. Contains the lowest evaluated price (TEP), provided that the TEP is not unbalanced and is fair and reasonable. The Government also reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, either before or after the closing date. 1. Requirement: This requirement is for W127/W221- FURNITURE at Wright Patterson Air Force Base in accordance with the Statement of Work (SOW). 2. Period of Performance: No later than 120 Days ADC. This is inclusive of in person post award site visit, material finish selection, furniture lead time and installation. 3. Provisions and Clauses: See solicitation attachment for applicable provisions and clauses that apply to this acquisition. Offerors shall complete and include in quotations all representations and certifications, as well as all fill-in provisions and clauses, contained within this solicitation. Additionally, quotations that contain pricing only with no description/detail of the equipment that will be provided will not be accepted or considered for award. NOTE: In accordance with deviation R-DFARS 252.204-7998(g), the offeror's quote submission legally binds and certifies that its SAM registration is current, complete, accurate, and has been updated within the preceding 12 months as of the offer's date. 4. Request for Information (RFIs): The Government will accept questions concerning this solicitation until 12 SEP 2026 at 2:00 PM EST. Email your questions on a .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls or .xlsx document to adam.holden.1@us.af.mil and jessica.stamper.2@us.af.mil. Any questions received after this date and time may not be considered. In accordance with Department of Defense cybersecurity requirements, contractors accessing government-furnished Computer-Aided Design (CAD) drawings must comply with NIST Special Publication (SP) 800?171, Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations, Level 1. The solicitation includes restricted CAD drawings showing furniture layouts only. These restricted drawings, with all base plans, reference layers, and sensitive spatial data removed, are available to all offerors as part of the solicitation package. Contractors that require access to the full CAD drawing sets, including base plans and associated layers necessary for detailed coordination, must submit a written request to the Contracting Officer and provide documentation or other evidence demonstrating current NIST SP 800?171 Level 1 compliance. Upon verification of NIST SP 800?171 Level 1 compliance, the Government will provide the full CAD drawing sets to the requesting contractor. Contractors that do not request full CAD drawings or do not demonstrate compliance will be limited to the restricted CAD drawings provided with the solicitation. 5. Quotes Due Date: Quotes must be submitted electronically to the Contract Specialist via e-mail at adam.holden.1 @us.af.mil and Contracting Officer at jessica.stamper.2@us.af.mil. Quotes must conform to the requirements of this solicitation and be received no later than 15 SEP 2026 at 12:00 PM EST. It is the responsibility of the offeror to ensure that the quote and its attachments are received. Any correspondence sent via e-mail must contain the subject line �FA8601-26-Q-0146 � W127/W221- FURNITURE� The entire quotation must be contained in a single e-mail that does not exceed 5 megabytes including attachments, if any. E-mails with compressed files are not permitted. Note that e-mail filters at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base are designed to filter e-mails without subject lines or with suspicious subject lines or contents (i.e., .exe or .zip files). Therefore, if the specified subject line is not included, the e-mail may not get through the e-mail filters. Also be advised that .zip or .exe files are not allowable attachments and may be deleted by the email filters at Wright-Patterson. If sending attachments with email, ensure only .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls or .xlsx documents are sent. The email filter may delete any other form of attachments. If a DoDSafe drop off is needed, please notify the contract specialist or contracting officer at least 48 hours before quotes are due. Any quotes received after designated closing date and time need not be considered. Quotes must include aggregate total of base plus all option year CLINS, if requested (IAW RFO 52.217-5 Evaluation of Options). All quotes shall be in whole dollars and conform to the Contract Line-Item Number (CLIN) structure of attached solicitation. 6. Notice to Vendor(s): All vendors must fully complete and return the 'Required Information Sheet' (attached to the solicitation) and return with their quotation. Additionally, quotations that contain pricing only with no description/detail of the supply/service that will be provided will not be accepted or considered for award. 7. Tariffs: In accordance with R-DFARS 252.225-7013, the contractor is prohibited from including any amount for customs duties on eligible items within the quote price. The claim for duty-free entry is restricted to supplies destined for government use, either as end items or as components thereof. The Government will provide assistance in the process of obtaining duty-free entry. 8. Period of Acceptance of Quotes: Offeror agrees to hold prices in its quote firm for 60 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of offers. 9. SAM Registration: Firms submitting a quote for the solicitation described herein, MUST be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database, or risk the quote as being non-responsive, regardless of the package being considered complete, timely or any other salient consideration. Information to register on SAM can be found at the web site, SAM.gov. 10. Mandatory Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Level 1 Assessment: In accordance with DFARS 252.204-7021 and DFARS 252.204-7025, a CMMC Level 1 assessment is a mandatory requirement for all offerors. To be eligible for contract award, offerors must demonstrate full compliance with the 15 basic safeguarding requirements outlined in FAR 52.240.93. The contractor is responsible for entering the assessment results into the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE), specifically within the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) module. Contract award cannot be made to any offeror

title: Mobile Command Post
description: The 87th Security Forces Squadron (SFS) at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst (JB MDL) requires a fully integrated, turnkey mobile command-and-control asset to support expanding Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) operations, search-and-rescue (SAR) missions, perimeter surveillance, and rapid incident command capabilities. The objective of this contract is the procurement, custom integration, testing, and delivery of one (1) brand-neutral, fully insulated, climate-controlled, and technology-equipped 6' x 12' enclosed trailer designed to serve as a mobile flight command station. The system must meet or exceed all salient physical, functional, and performance characteristics outlined in Section 3 of this document to ensure operational readiness and safety. Please see the attached SOW for more information.

title: Chemical Nutrient Analysis Service
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Natick Division, in support of the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC), Soldier Sustainment Directorate (SSD) / Combat Feeding Division (CFD) located in Natick, MA 01760, has a requirement for nutrient analysis services for the U.S. Army Combat Feeding Division. The Combat Feeding Division�s Nutrient Analysis Laboratory (NAL) currently has multiple samples to analyze for nutritional content. The CFD, part of the U.S. Army DEVCOM-SC, is the Department of Defense�s centralized source for all research, development, engineering, and integration of joint service combat rations, food service equipment and field feeding systems. CFD�s primary mission is to ensure Warfighters have the tactical, nutritional and logistical advantage required to survive and win on the battlefield. Although CFD already has an in-house Nutrient Analysis Lab (NAL), there is currently a short-term need to outsource select nutrient analysis services for ingredients and ration components. The contractor shall provide laboratory nutrient analysis testing on provided food samples. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercially available services prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. Request For Proposal (RFP) number is: W911QY-26-R-CHEMICAL-NUTRIENT-ANALYSIS. The Government intends to award a single, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract as a result of this solicitation. All timely offers will be considered, and proposal submission shall be in accordance with Submission Instructions contained herein. Evaluation factors are Technical Capability, Price, and Past Performance. The Government intends to make award to the Offeror whose proposal represents the Best Value to the Government. This requirement is set for full and open competition. This is not set-aside to small businesses. The NAICS code is 541380 - Testing Laboratories and Services. The small business size standard is $19M. The Army�s Office for Small Business Programs concurs with the full and open competition determination. Incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2025-01. FAR Clauses 52.212-1 through 52.212-5 and DFARS 52.212-7001, Contract Terms and Conditions Required to Implement Statutes or Executive Orders Applicable to Defense Acquisitions of Commercial Items (see www.acquisition.gov) apply to this procurement. Contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov) to be eligible for award. Instructions for registration are available at the website. Any additional contract requirement(s) or terms and conditions determined by the Contracting Officer to be necessary for this acquisition and consistent with customary commercial practices shall apply. Submission Instructions: All Offerors shall submit a proposal consisting of three (3) sections. These three (3) sections shall be labeled; Section I � Technical Proposal; Section II � Pricing Proposal; and Section III � Past Performance. No Pricing Information shall be submitted in Section I. Evaluation will be in accordance with FAR 52.212-2 Evaluation--Commercial Items and Commercial Services. (a) The Government intends to award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to this solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: I. Technical capability of services offered to meet Government requirements: Requirements: The contractor shall be able to analyze samples for the analytes in Table 1 (See Attached Statement of Work for Table 1) with the preferred methods listed below or equivalent* with the listed limits of quantification (LOQ). The main analytes that will be requested are 1) selenium, 2) vitamin B12 (cobalamin) and 3) total dietary fiber. However, the contractor must also have the ability to analyze for any of the other analytes listed below, in case CFD has a need to have those analytes determined as well. This SOW is for an indeterminate quantity of samples (25-100), up to $25K during the period of performance. No more than 25 samples would be sent at one time. Analyses and results shall be completed and delivered to the government no later than 14 calendar days after receipt of samples. Contractor shall prepare a data report for each set of samples that has been analyzed to include sample name/ID, method used, results, units of measure, limit of quantification and date of analysis. *If the contractor proposes to use a different method than the preferred methods listed, than that method must be specified in their proposal as well as the LOQ of that method. If the method is not an industry standard method (publicly available), then please attach a copy of the method in the proposal. During market research the price ranges in Table 2 (See Attached Statement of Work for Table 2) were determined to be reasonable per analyte (dependent on the method proposed). Contractor�s proposals must include the cost/test and the proposed method w/ LOQ. A cost/test can be outside of this range, but the proposals will be evaluated based on the demonstrated ability of the contractor to meet the requirements, proposed methods with LOQ and the cost/test. a. General Requirements In-House Capacity: The contractor must have the in-house capacity (personnel, equipment, etc.) to perform the analyses requested. Contractors acting as pass throughs to larger labs will not be accepted. Accreditation: The contractor shall maintain active ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for the duration of the contract. The accreditation scope must cover the specific nutritional tests requested. Analytical Methodology: All testing must utilize validated, industry-standard methods (e.g., AOAC International, USP, AACC, or equivalent recognized methods). If an alternative method is used, the contractor must provide scientific validation prior to testing. Sample Custody & Tracking: The contractor must maintain a documented chain of custody from sample receipt at the facility until final disposal. Communication & Support: The contractor shall designate a primary point of contact (POC) or project manager to handle inquiries, clarify test results, and resolve sample receipt issues within 24 hours. Storage Conditions: Upon receipt, the contractor shall store all samples under the conditions specified by the government (e.g., ambient, refrigerated at 4�C, or frozen at -20�C) to prevent nutrient degradation before analysis. Sample Retention: The contractor must retain the remaining homogenized sample material for a minimum of 30 calendar days after the final report is delivered, allowing the government to request re-testing if anomalies are found. Disposal: After the 30-day retention period, the contractor shall safely dispose of the food samples in accordance with local environmental regulations at no additional cost to the government. b. Specific Requirements See Attached Statement of Work for Table containing the Specific Requirements and additional details. II. Price: Reference Table 1 & 2 in the attached SOW. III. Past Performance: Offerors are reminded that while the Government may elect to consider data obtained from other sources, the burden of providing thorough and complete past performance information rests with the Offeror. Offerors shall submit three (3) recent and relevant past performance examples performed within the last three years. Each example shall not exceed two (2) pages and shall include the following: 1. Contract number, date of award, order number if applicable, CAGE code, DUNS number, and North American Industry Classification

title: COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE FOR COMBINED ARMS VIRTUAL ENVIRONMENT TRAINER (CAVE) UPGRADE
description: ***THIS IS A COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE*** SPECIAL NOTICE: Combined Sources Sought and Notice of Intent to Sole Source This is a Combined Sources Sought Notice and Notice of Intent to Sole Source published in accordance with FAR 5.201 and FAR Part 10. The Department of War/ Naval Air Warfare Center Training Systems Division (NAWCTSD) intends to negotiate a sole-source contract with Battlespace Simulations LLC under the authority of FAR 6.302-1. This notice is published for market research purposes to determine if other responsible sources exist that can satisfy this requirement BACKGROUND The Naval Air Warfare Center Training Systems Division (NAWCTSD), Orlando, FL intends to sole source the effort to restore non-mission-capable Portable Lightweight Designator/Rangefinder (PLDR) and Common Laser Range Finder - Integrated Capability (CLRF-IC) targeting assets to a fully operational, calibrated, and deployable status to Battlespace Simulations LLC (BSI) (CAGE code 4KC80) of Lakewood Ranch, FL under the authority of 10 USC 2304 (c) (1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1. BSI is the developer of the specialized software and custom firmware plug-in configurations integrated into these tactical units, and possesses the exclusive proprietary source code, technical data rights, and certified optical calibration chambers required to align the optics and certify that the lasers meet original MIL-SPEC eye-safe parameters. The Government does not have and cannot provide data rights to any software components that would be necessary to perform this upgrade. In order to comply with PGI 206.302-1, the Government is seeking information on the availability of potential comparable sources to upgrade the existing CAVE training systems capability located at Expeditionary Warfare Training Group, Pacific (EWTGPAC), Naval Amphibious Base (NAB) Coronado in San Diego, California (CA). BSI is the only responsible source capable of satisfying this requirement because they hold the proprietary technical data, software rights, and specialized calibration tooling necessary to return these military unique targeting systems to a mission-capable state. The updated hardware components utilized during the refurbishment process require a proprietary software firmware plug-in developed exclusively by BSI. Only BSI's engineering team possesses the proprietary source code and technical data rights to configure, install, and test this software on the PLDR and CLRF-IC systems. No other vendor can provide or support this critical interface software. HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS NOTICE In responding to this notice, please DO NOT PROVIDE PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. Submit the response by email to the Primary Point of Contact and, if specified, to the Secondary Point of Contact listed in this notice as soon as possible, and preferably before the closing date and time of this notice. Please review the attached PDF file for further details. IMPORTANT NOTES The information received in response to this notice will be reviewed and considered so that NAWCTSD may appropriately solicit for its requirements in the near future. This notice should not be construed as a commitment by NAWCTSD to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. This notice is not a request for a quotation. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotations. No award will be made as a result of this notice. NAWCTSD is not responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. NAWCTSD reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and appropriate. Thank you for taking the time to submit a response to this request!

title: Laboratory Analysis - Phase II Environmental Site Assessment - Fort DuPont, Delaware City, DE
description: Introduction: It is the intent of the Government to award a sole source purchase order for analytical laboratory services from Alpha Analytical as cited in the attached Sole Source Justification. Under an Interagency Agreement, the U.S. Departme nt of Transportation John A. Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe Center) is providing support to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Targeted Brownfields Assessments (TBA) Program. As part of this effort, a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) that includes a requirement for laboratory analysis will be conducted at the Fort DuPont Parade Ground (the Site) located at 260 Old Elm Ave, Delaware City, Delaware. Background: The objective of this Phase II ESA investigation is to determine if known contamination stemming from former military operations at the Fort DuPont property has impacted soil or groundwater at the Parade Ground (OU-9). Laboratory analytical data from soil and groundwater samples obtained through the advancement of soil borings and the installation of groundwater monitoring wells will be collected. Analytical results will be compared the Human Health and Ecological Screening Levels published in the Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control (DNREC) Hazardous Substance Cleanup Act (HSCA) Screening Level Table Guidance Appendix A tables. Soil samples will be compared to the Soil (Direct Contract) HSCA Human Health Screening Levels and the Ecological Surface Soil Screening Levels. Groundwater samples will be compared to the Groundwater HSCA Human Health Screening Levels. Tasks to be Performed: The Phase II ESA investigation includes the Contractor tasks listed below. The Contractor shall conduct all work in accordance with Federal, State and local requirements. Where inconsistencies exist, the Contractor shall follow the most stringent requirements. 1) Sample Containers, Handling, and Delivery: The Contractor shall provide the appropriate sample containers, disposable volatiles samplers, preservatives, pre-printed labels, and analyte-free water required for the analyses listed below. These are to be delivered by the Contractor to the project site location. Sample collection and handling will be performed by Volpe personnel. The laboratory shall provide a daily local courier to transport the samples from the Site to the laboratory over an anticipated three days of sampling. Whenever possible, the Contractor shall minimize the number of sample containers by combining compatible analyses into a single container, as allowed by EPA methods and laboratory standard operating procedures. 2) Sample Analysis: Metals, Cyanide, VOCs, SVOCs, TPH-DRO, TPH GRO, PCBs, Pesticides, VOC Trip Blank, Metals, Cyanide, VOCs, SVOCs, TPH-DRO, TPH GRO, PCBs, Pesticides.

description: Concept Papers - Submissions will be accepted from July 15, 2024 � Septemb 30, 2026. In response to this BAA solicitation, Concept Papers must be submitted to: VHASuicidePreventionBAA@va.gov As an innovation engine within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the vision of the VA Innovation Ecosystem (VHAIE) is a VA innovating at the forefront of science and research, service delivery, and employee empowerment. title: CFTC LAZ Executive Parking
description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) intends to issue a sole source purchase order to LAZ Parking Ltd. title: PC-12 Hangar Support
description: NASA/AFRC has a requirement for facilities and utilities necessary to support PC-12 aircraft ground and flight operations during the QUARC laser communications campaign. The scope includes hangar access, servicing utilities, secure office and storage space, internet connectivity, fuel support for ground equipment, and personnel access coordination. NASA/AFRC intends to issue a sole source contract to acquire the services from JetsFBO. NASA requires contractor-provided hangar facilities, utilities, and support at Cleveland Hopkins International Airport (KCLE) in Cleveland, Ohio. The purpose of this effort is to ensure safe, continuous, and efficient PC-12 ground and flight operations in support of the Quantum Aerospace Communication (QUARC) mission objectives. Hangar location for the PC-12 QUARC laser communications campaign must be at KCLE. The QUARC payload systems need to link-up to NASA Glenn Research Center (GRC) ground stations (line of sight) during integration and ground testing operations. The Government intends to acquire a commercial product or service using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to Jamill Richter, jamill.m.richter@nasa.gov and Nikki Terranova, nikki.terranova@nasa.gov not later than September 15, 2026 at 10:00am PT. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A decision by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at : https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf

title: Replace Substation Alpha Relay B11912
description: This is a solicitation for the requirement of properly replacing the Substation Alpha Feeder Protection Relays at Building 11912 on Dyess AFB. The Contractor shall install (2) NEW GE 850 Feeder Protection Relays which are provided by the Government. The contractor shall install and wire in (2) new Feeder Protection Relays in accordance with NEC/ NETA standards. The Contractor shall program the (2) new Feeder protection relays to match programming of the previously installed GE 760 relays, via settings provided by the Electrical shop and test functionality without load. title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION -ADVANCE NOTICE TO INDUSTRY: Potential Use of Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for the Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) Program at Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM)
description: 1. NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market intelligence and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a formal Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Request for Qualifications (RFQ), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not award any agreement or contract as a result of this notice, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Submission of a response does not obligate the Government in any way, and will not affect a firm's ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. While Other Transaction (OT) Agreements executed under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a are not subject to standard FAR-based small business set-aside regulations, the Government is highly interested in understanding the size, demographics, and capabilities of the interested industrial base. 2. PURPOSE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, on behalf of Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), is conducting market intelligence to explore the use of Other Transaction Authority (OTA) under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a to provide an innovative, programmatic approach to delivering its Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) program. 3. PROGRAM OVERVIEW The scope of the JBLM FSRM Program includes operational facilities, training sites, administrative spaces, barracks/troop housing, utility infrastructure systems (HVAC, electrical, fire protection), and site work for JBLM Garrison facilities Projects will span multiple facility types across JBLM (Lewis Main, McChord Field, and Yakima Training Center). Projects will be primarily general construction activities including but not limited to: renovation, repairs, building expansions, and pre-engineered buildings (not to exceed the statutory limit for new construction), or repair by replacement. Scope may also include preventative maintenance, environmental abatement (e.g., asbestos and lead-based paint abatement), erosion control, and earthwork. Construction situations may include but are not limited to: civil, mechanical, plumbing, structural, electrical, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), fire protection systems, communications systems, and anti-terrorism and force protection. 4. POTENTIAL ACQUISITION STRATEGY The Government intends to establish a Master OT Agreement framework with the following characteristics: � Aggregate Program Value: Approximately $100 Million. � Structure: A single Master OT Agreement under which a pool of multiple pre-qualified design-build (or equivalent) teams will be established. � Period of Performance: A 5-year base period with the potential to extend to a total of 7 years. � Work Packages: Individual FSRM projects will be packaged and assigned to teams within the pre-qualified pool over the life of the agreement. � Project Delivery Methods: Individual work packages may be executed utilizing Progressive Design-Build (PDB), Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR), or other collaborative, fast-tracked commercial delivery methods tailored to the specific project. � Anticipated Two-Step Selection Process: To minimize bid-and-proposal costs for industry, the Government intends to utilize a streamlined, Qualifications-Based Selection (QBS) process to select the pool of partners: Step 1 (Request for Qualifications): Proposers submit a highly concise Statement of Qualifications (SOQ) focusing on team capability, alternative delivery past performance, and collaborative philosophy. No pricing will be evaluated. Step 2 (Pitch Presentations): Shortlisted firms will be invited to participate in confidential, interactive "Pitch Presentations" and workshops to evaluate team chemistry, real-time problem-solving, and open-book commercial capability. 5. ANTICIPATED INDUSTRY DAY USACE Seattle District anticipates hosting an Industry Day in the Seattle area on or about 20 October 2026. The Industry Day is intended to: � Provide an overview of the JBLM FSRM OTA concept, anticipated Master Agreement structure, and potential scope � Share the Government�s current thinking on delivery methods (including but not limited to Progressive Design-Build) � Obtain industry feedback on commercial practices, teaming, pricing approaches, risk allocation, and barriers to participation � Allow one-on-one or small-group discussions with interested firms (as capacity permits) Exact date, time, location, registration instructions, and agenda will be published in a subsequent notice (SAM.gov and/or direct distribution to respondents to this RFI). Firms that respond to this RFI will be prioritized for Industry Day communications. 6. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested parties are requested to submit responses by completing the online questionnaire at: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/FeJXcQu89F The questionnaire is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market intelligence and addresses industry capability, experience, technical capabilities, construction considerations, and recommended OTA and commercial practices. If necessary, interested parties may also submit a brief capabilities statement containing relevant information not otherwise addressed in the questionnaire. Capability statements shall not exceed 5 pages in length. The Government requests that firms avoid duplicating information already provided through the questionnaire. Supplemental capability statements are requested to be submitted via email to the individual(s) listed below no later than 10:00 AM Pacific Time on 15 September 2026. Late responses may still be considered at the Government�s discretion but are not guaranteed review prior to strategy finalization. Jeffrey Ross, Contracting Officer Brett Vegeto, Contracting Officer JBLM Special Projects Branch Contracting Division, Seattle District, Northwestern Division Email: jeffrey.a.ross@usace.army.mil Email: brett.s.vegeto@usace.army.mil Subject line: �RFI Response � JBLM FSRM Other Transaction Authority � [Firm Name]� The Government welcomes candid industry feedback and recommendations regarding commercial practices, agreement terms, project phasing, risk sharing, governance, pricing approaches, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of this project under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. Note: Do not submit proprietary trade secrets, protected technologies, or classified information in your response. All feedback received will be handled as public market research to shape the Government's final acquisition approach.

title: Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Innovation Ecosystem (VHAIE); Broad Agency Announcement (BAA); Suicide Prevention
description: Concept Papers - Submissions will be accepted from July 15, 2024 � August 15, 2025. In response to this BAA solicitation, Concept Papers must be submitted to: VHASuicidePreventionBAA@va.gov As an innovation engine within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the vision of the VA Innovation Ecosystem (VHAIE) is a VA innovating at the forefront of science and research, service delivery, and employee empowerment. VHAIE leads this vision through development of organizational capability, delivery of operational breakthroughs, and by driving futures. VHAIE is committed to developing and employing agile mechanisms that allow VA to source incremental and transformational innovations to best serve Veterans and their families. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) opportunity seeks to source and fund early-stage research, development, prototyping, and piloting with an overall goal of moving forward the state of the art. VHAIE invites all potential offerors (including private sector companies, non-profits, and institutions of higher learning) to contribute ideas for innovations in SUICIDE prevention, care coordination, and treatment that significantly increase Veteran access to services, reduce or control costs of delivering those services, enhance the performance of VA operations, and improve the quality of service that Veterans and their families receive.

The U.S. Government reimburses DBA insurance carriers for claims paid in connection with injuries or deaths from war hazards as defined and covered by the War Hazards Compensation Act. Santa Clara St, San Jose, California. The response to this RFI should provide OCAO management with an understanding of the contractor�s experience and the range of services provided. Demonstrated expertise in working with the GSA, OMB and Congress for federal office space leasing acquisition. Expert level experience in strategic planning and programming, conceptual and schematic design, design development, construction and contract documents, and project administration.
